absent: IRQ remapping prepare, enable, disable and reenable protocols and error code meanings beyond success versus negative failure.
Legacy PIC mask and restore semantics and required ordering relative to IOAPIC operations.
IOAPIC hardware entry layout beyond the masked flag and the read and write primitives.
APIC driver fields for destination mode, hooks and maximum identifier, and fixmap handling.
Hypervisor extended mode availability and extended destination contracts.
Local APIC register offsets and bit definitions for spurious, vector entries, error status, service state and timer.
MSR bit definitions for base, architecture capabilities and disable status beyond the names used.
Boot option registration strings and parsing context for local APIC and timer options.
Tracepoint payloads for spurious and error entry and exit.
Syscore lifecycle, threading guarantees and power management activation details.
DMI matching semantics beyond the single known vendor product entry.
Deadline timer validation and per processor clock event setup contracts.

findings.text: Boot time coordination service for interrupt remapping together with extended APIC mode selection. It preserves IOAPIC routing state so that an unsuccessful activation can leave prior routing restorable, and it leaves legacy masking and processor interrupt state restored on all paths. It declines early when IOAPIC setup was skipped.

Extended APIC control uses four ordered markers where the two lower values mean inactive and the two upper values mean active. Activation moves from the off marker to the on marker and is ignored from any other marker. Deactivation is ignored unless currently at or above the on marker, then moves to the disabled marker and clears the mode flag.

Disabling extended mode is refused for processors whose identifier cannot be represented in legacy width, ending in a fatal halt, and is refused with a warning when hardware reports a locked configuration. A boot option requesting no extended mode applies the same identifier and lock checks before clearing the capability and forcing the disabled marker.

Selection between remapped and nonremapped extended mode depends on the remap outcome. Nonremapped use on bare metal is rejected unless a hypervisor facility reports availability, and physical addressing is then forced with a bounded maximum identifier. Hypervisor extended destination support widens that bound substantially.

Capability register accessor that returns zero when the processor lacks the architecture capabilities feature and otherwise returns the current register contents. It underpins locked extended APIC detection without faulting on older processors.

Low level enable and disable operations against the APIC base register are idempotent and tolerate repeated invocation. The disable path first checks for local APIC presence and current enablement, temporarily clears both enable controls before restoring legacy mode, while the enable path only sets the extended control when not already set. Alternate build variants provide empty operations.

Boot time limit setter recording the highest usable APIC identifier and, when the active APIC driver offers a corresponding hook, propagating that bound to the driver maximum. It allows nonremapped extended mode to exclude identifiers that IOAPIC and MSI cannot address.

IOAPIC handling maintains a saved copy per controller per pin. Saving copies current hardware entries and reports memory shortage when storage is absent but continues across controllers. Masking rewrites only entries observed unmasked in the saved copy, leaving already masked entries untouched. Restoration rewrites every saved entry unconditionally and always reports success.

Interrupt register view provides two overlays of the same storage: an array of machine words sized to cover all interrupt bits and an array of thirty two bit hardware registers. The bit count derives from the register count times the width of one register, and the word count derives from that bit count divided by the width of one machine word.

Application processor setup entry invoked during secondary bringup to initialize the local interrupt controller and then complete local setup. It has no return value and performs the same two phase local initialization on every secondary.

Early detection records whether firmware already enabled extended mode and whether hardware reports locked status, distinguishing a locked active marker from an unlocked active marker. Secondary setup aligns secondaries with the boot processor choice, warns on lock mismatch, enables when the global state is active and otherwise ensures firmware enabled state is turned off. A build without extended support instead disables the local APIC entirely when firmware enabled it.

Local APIC discovery offers a minimal presence check and a fuller vendor gated probe. The fuller probe accepts specific AMD, Hygon and Intel families, honors a disabled flag and a force enable request, verifies the feature flag and base address, and activates power management on success. Mapping initialization announces deadline timer availability, bypasses legacy mapping when extended mode is active, and otherwise falls back to detection with facility disable on failure.

Verification requires the processor feature flag to be set after enablement, updates the boot capability, adopts any firmware programmed base address on later processors, and registers that address. Forced enablement rewrites the base register only on later processors when firmware left it disabled, preserving other controls while setting enable and address, and then delegates to verification.

Interrupt vector entries are provided for a general spurious handler parameterized by vector, a dedicated spurious vector entry fixed to the architectural spurious value, and a dedicated error entry. All funnel through common spurious or error logic with tracing on entry and exit.

Spurious accounting increments a dedicated counter and marks it visible before any acknowledgement decision. The architectural spurious value is never acknowledged. Other vectors consult the corresponding in service bit and acknowledge only when that bit shows pending, with distinct reporting for acknowledged versus not pending cases.

Error handling tickles the error status register before sampling when the local vector table is large enough to avoid a historic erratum, then samples, acknowledges, counts a dedicated error counter and decodes only the low byte as up to eight independent causes. Reporting is done through debug channels rather than normal logs.
Per processor interrupt statistics helper that increments the selected counter and marks that counter index for display. It is used for spurious and error accounting and has no failure modes.

Boot processor disconnect restores compatibility wiring by enabling the spurious vector entry with a fixed low vector while preserving other controls, then programs local vector entries for external and nonmaskable delivery with edge active high semantics and cleared mask and pending state, except that one setup mode leaves the first entry masked. A legacy picture mode on one word size takes an early alternate path that returns without further programming.

Message signaled interrupt composition zeroes the message then fills fixed delivery, vector from the interrupt configuration, logical destination mode from the active driver, and split destination identifier with low bits always in the address low part. High identifier bits use an IOMMU only field when remapping is involved, otherwise an optional virtual extended field within bounds, with a one time warning when the identifier exceeds legacy width and no extended path applies. Extraction recombines low and optional high parts under caller control.
Uniprocessor late initialization entry that does nothing in picture mode and otherwise arms the per processor clock event device. It runs once during boot after interrupt mode is known.

Power state container records an ownership flag plus saved values for identification, task priority, logical and destination format, spurious vector, timer initial and divide settings, all local vector entries including timer performance and error, and optionally thermal and machine check entries when the vector table is large enough. Suspend and resume operations are registered as system core callbacks through a small ops and core pair, with registration occurring only when local APIC capability is present.

Suspend is a no operation unless this software enabled the local controller, otherwise it snapshots registers according to vector table size and then under disabled interrupts masks IOAPIC, disables the local controller and disables remapping. Resume is likewise gated, quiets IOAPIC and legacy sources under disabled interrupts, restores extended or legacy base mode with firmware re enable detection, rewrites saved registers in an order that keeps error reporting masked until cleared, and finally re enables remapping with knowledge of extended mode.

Clustered chassis detection uses a one shot desktop management check for a single known vendor product pair. The first query runs the table scan and caches the outcome, later queries reuse the cached flag, and the setter ignores repeat matches once the flag is set.

Boot option handlers disable the local APIC facility and clear its capability, record permission for the local timer in low power idle, or disable the local timer through two spelling variants. All run early during option parsing and unconditionally report success.

Remapping plus extended mode activation holds processor interrupts disabled across legacy masking, IOAPIC masking, remap enablement attempt and mode selection, restoring prior interrupt state only after legacy masks are restored and IOAPIC state is either kept or restored.

Suspend and resume paths hold processor interrupts disabled while masking external sources and toggling local controller and remapping state, ensuring no interrupt is serviced from a partially saved or partially restored controller.

Attempting to leave extended mode with an identifier outside legacy representability halts the system, while locked hardware or firmware re enablement across suspend produces warnings and preserves the active mode. A lock mismatch between boot and secondary processors is warned about because a later disable attempt on a locked secondary could fault. Nonremapped MSI identifiers beyond legacy width trigger a one time warning.

Spurious handling never acknowledges the architectural spurious vector but may acknowledge genuinely pending vectored entries after consulting service state, so callers must not assume acknowledgement always occurs. Error handling clears status twice around restoration of the masked error vector during resume and during live handling, requiring the large vector table guard to avoid corrupting status on affected processors.

Legacy addressable APIC identifier bound is 255, with disable and option handling treating that value and above as incompatible with legacy mode. Nonremapped extended mode with hypervisor extended destination support widens the bound to 32767 and permits virtual extended identifiers below 32768.
Interrupt register file sizing uses 32 bits per register, with total bits equal to register count times 32 and machine word count equal to total bits divided by bits per machine word.

Architectural spurious vector value is 0xFF with a low nibble value 0xF used when re enabling the spurious entry during compatibility restore. Error decoding uses only the low 8 bits. MSI low destination carries 8 bits with legacy limit 0xFF and vectored spurious decoding uses 5 bit grouping within the service registers.

Public boot and secondary interfaces comprise secondary local setup, extended mode secondary synchronization, early extended mode detection, local mapping initialization, forced local enablement, legacy compatibility disconnect, and clustered chassis query. All are intended for boot or secondary bringup callers and assume single threaded early context except the chassis query which is safe to repeat.

Public IOAPIC snapshot services allow saving, masking and restoring all controller entries across mode transitions and suspend. Public MSI helpers construct a message from interrupt configuration and extract the destination identifier with caller controlled extended handling.

When extended support is not compiled in, the mode selection helper and low level toggles compile to empty operations with no state effects, while early detection instead reports missing support and disables the local facility.
